name: btop
author: blabbleu
description: A btop-style system monitor as its own WebUI page (rail icon). CPU graph with per-core meters and temps, memory/swap, disks with I/O, network up/down graphs, a Hermes box that groups agent/WebUI/cron/MCP/swe-pilot processes, and a sortable, filterable process table with tree view, details and signals. Data comes from a stdlib-only loopback sidecar reading /proc.

post_install.summary: Start the bundled sidecar as the WebUI user: mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user; copy sidecar/hermes-btop-sidecar.service there; systemctl --user daemon-reload; systemctl --user enable --now hermes-btop-sidecar (or run python3 -S sidecar.py). Then approve the proxy in Settings → Extensions → Diagnostics → Loopback sidecars. Requires WebUI auth on (token-v1).

storage.note: Only the extension-owned key 'prefs' via hermesExt storage; no raw localStorage keys.

filesystem.note: Sidecar reads (never writes): /proc/<pid>/{stat,status,io,cmdline} plus fd count and cwd/exe links; /proc/{stat,meminfo,net/dev,diskstats,loadavg,uptime,cpuinfo,self/mounts}; /sys/class/hwmon; statvfs on real filesystem mounts (own worker, 1.5 s timeout per mount); /etc/os-release, /run/systemd/container, /.dockerenv (existence), /etc/passwd via getpwuid; WebUI's token file <state>/sidecar-auth/btop.token. It does not read other processes' environ. Command lines are masked per argv element before leaving the sidecar; masking is best-effort, not a guarantee. Signals (TERM/INT/HUP/KILL/STOP/CONT) are pinned to the confirmed process via start time + pidfd and act with the sidecar user's privileges; BTOP_SIGNALS=0 disables them.
